explain.say: Today we are learning some useful lab skills for chemistry.

draw.text: Lab Skills: Reflux, Distillation, Recrystallisation, MP

explain.say: Reflux involves boiling a reaction mixture at a constant temperature.
Distillation separates liquids with different boiling points.
Recrystallisation purifies a solid by dissolving it in hot solvent.

items: Dissolve solid in minimum hot solvent

explain.say: The melting point range tells us about the purity of a solid compound.
In the lab, we use these techniques to isolate pure substances.

faq.q: Why do I need to use reflux in the lab?
faq.a: Reflux allows a reaction to proceed for a long time without losing the solvent to evaporation. This keeps the reaction mixture at a constant boiling point.
asks: What is the purpose of the condenser?
How do I prevent solvent loss during heating?

faq.q: When should I use distillation instead of reflux?
faq.a: You use distillation when you want to separate a liquid mixture into its individual components. Reflux is for keeping the mixture together while heating.
asks: What is the difference between the two techniques?

faq.q: How does recrystallisation actually purify a solid?
faq.a: It relies on the fact that solubility changes with temperature. The impurities remain dissolved even when the main substance crystallises out.
asks: Why do I cool the solution slowly?
What property of the solid is used here?

faq.q: What does a wide melting point range mean for my sample?
faq.a: A wide melting point range indicates that your solid is impure. The impurities lower and broaden the temperature at which it melts.
asks: Is a sharp melting point always good?
What causes the melting point to change?

faq.a: They are essential when the starting materials are mixtures, and you need to obtain a pure product for further study. They are fundamental separation methods.
asks: Can I skip these steps sometimes?
Are there simpler ways to purify things?

facts: Reflux uses a condenser to cool vapours back to liquid.
Distillation separates liquids based on boiling point differences.
Recrystallisation requires the solute to be insoluble at low temperatures.
A pure solid has a sharp, characteristic melting point range.

quiz.say: If you are separating ethanol and water, which technique is most appropriate?
quiz.why: Distillation is specifically designed to separate liquids that have different boiling points.

wrong.0: Reflux keeps the mixture boiling without separating the components.
wrong.1: Recrystallisation is used for purifying solid compounds, not liquids.
wrong.2: Melting point only measures the transition temperature of a solid.

quiz.say: To purify a solid, you dissolve it in hot solvent and cool it. What is this process called?
quiz.why: Recrystallisation uses temperature-dependent solubility to leave impurities behind.

wrong.1: Distillation separates liquids, not solids dissolved in solvents.
wrong.2: Reflux is a heating technique, not a purification method for solids.
wrong.3: Melting point is a measurement, not a purification technique itself.

quiz.say: A substance melts sharply at 150 degrees Celsius. What does this suggest about the sample?
quiz.why: A sharp melting point range is characteristic of a pure crystalline substance.

wrong.0: Mixtures usually have a broad melting range.
wrong.1: Volatility relates to boiling, not melting point sharpness.
wrong.2: Refluxing is used for reactions, not for determining purity.
